title: Penguins of Antarctica
summary: How penguins swim, stay warm, raise their chicks, find food, and hide from predators in icy Antarctica, and how melting sea ice affects them.
poll: Penguins are better suited to their home than almost any other animal.

versions.title: Birds of the Ice
versions.text:
Far to the south is a land of ice. It is Antarctica. It is the coldest place on Earth.

Some birds live here. They are penguins. Penguins can not fly. Their wings are flippers. They swim with them.

How do they stay warm? They have a thick coat of fat. They have lots of feathers. The feathers keep out the cold and wet. In a storm, they huddle. They stand close in a big group. They take turns in the warm middle.

The biggest kind is the emperor penguin. It is as tall as a small child. The mom lays one egg. She gives it to the dad. He holds it on his feet. A flap of warm skin keeps it safe. He does not eat for two months! The mom goes to the sea to eat. She comes back when the chick hatches. Then both feed it.

Penguins eat fish and squid. They eat krill, too. Krill are small, like shrimp. Some dive very deep.

Their backs are black. Their fronts are white. This helps them hide in the sea. Seals and whales hunt them.

Now the sea ice is melting. Penguins need it. Experts count them from space!

versions.title: Birds of the Ice
versions.text:
Far to the south is a land of ice called Antarctica. It is the coldest place on Earth. Strong winds blow there. In winter, the sun does not come up for weeks.

Some birds live in this cold land. They are penguins. Penguins can not fly. Their wings are flat flippers. They use them to swim fast under the water.

How do penguins stay warm? They have a thick layer of fat. They also have lots of small feathers packed close. The feathers keep out the cold and the wet. In a storm, penguins huddle. They stand close in a big group. They take turns in the warm middle.

The biggest kind is the emperor penguin. It is as tall as a small child. The mother lays one egg and gives it to the father. He holds the egg on his feet. A flap of warm skin covers it. He does not eat for about two months! The mother goes to the sea to eat. She comes back when the chick hatches. Then both parents feed it.

Penguins eat fish, squid, and krill. Krill are tiny sea animals that look like shrimp. Some penguins dive very deep to find food.

A penguin has a black back and a white front. This helps it hide in the sea. Seals and whales hunt penguins.

Today, some sea ice is melting. Penguins need that ice. Scientists now count penguins from space!

versions.title: Penguins: Birds of the Ice
versions.text:
Far to the south is a land of ice and snow called Antarctica. It is the coldest and windiest place on Earth. In winter, it can be colder than minus 40 degrees. The sun does not rise for weeks.

Some birds make this land their home. They are penguins. Penguins cannot fly, but they are great swimmers. Their wings are stiff flippers that push them through the water.

How do penguins stay warm? They have a thick layer of fat under their skin. They also have lots of small feathers packed tightly together. The feathers keep out the cold and the water. When a storm comes, penguins huddle. Hundreds stand close in a big group. They take turns moving into the warm middle.

The largest kind is the emperor penguin. It is about as tall as a small child. The mother lays one egg and passes it to the father. He holds it on his feet, under a warm flap of skin. He does not eat for about two months! The mother goes to the sea to feed. She comes back when the chick hatches. Then both parents feed it.

Penguins eat fish, squid, and krill. Krill are tiny sea animals that look like shrimp. Some penguins dive very deep to catch food.

A penguin has a black back and a white front. This helps it hide from seals and whales that hunt it.

Today, some of the sea ice is melting. Penguins need this ice to raise their chicks. Scientists now count penguins in photos taken from space.

versions.title: Penguins: Birds of the Ice
versions.text:
At the bottom of the world lies Antarctica, a land covered in thick ice. It is the coldest and windiest place on Earth. In winter, the air can drop below minus 40 degrees, and the sun does not rise for weeks.

Yet some birds live here. They are penguins. Penguins cannot fly, but they are amazing swimmers. Their wings are stiff flippers that push them through the water.

How do penguins survive the cold? First, they have a thick layer of fat under their skin. Second, they have many small feathers packed tightly together. These feathers keep out the cold and the water. When a storm blows in, penguins huddle. Hundreds of birds press close together. They take turns moving into the warm middle of the group.

The largest kind is the emperor penguin, which is about as tall as a small child. In winter, the mother lays one egg and passes it to the father. He balances the egg on his feet, under a warm flap of skin. He eats nothing for about two months! Meanwhile, the mother travels to the sea to feed. She returns when the chick hatches, and then both parents feed it.

Penguins eat fish, squid, and krill. Krill are tiny sea animals that look like shrimp. Some penguins dive very deep to catch their food.

A penguin's black back and white front help it hide in the sea. This keeps it safer from seals and whales that hunt it.

Today, some of the sea ice is melting. Emperor penguins need this ice to raise their chicks. To keep track of them, scientists now count penguins in pictures taken from space.

versions.title: Penguins of Antarctica
versions.text:
At the bottom of the world lies Antarctica, a continent buried under thick ice. It is the coldest and windiest place on Earth. In winter, the air can fall below minus 40 degrees Celsius, and the sun does not rise for weeks.

Yet some birds live here. They are penguins. Penguins cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers. Their wings have become stiff flippers that push them through the water.

Penguins have several ways to survive the cold. Under their skin is a thick layer of fat called blubber. On top are many small feathers packed tightly together, which keep out the wind and water. During storms, penguins huddle. Hundreds of birds press together, and they take turns moving into the warm center of the group.

The largest kind is the emperor penguin, which stands more than one meter tall. In winter, the mother lays a single egg and passes it to the father. He balances it on his feet, under a warm fold of skin. He eats nothing for about two months! Meanwhile, the mother travels to the sea to feed. She returns when the chick hatches, and then both parents feed it.

Penguins eat fish, squid, and krill, which are tiny animals that look like shrimp. Emperor penguins can dive more than 500 meters deep.

A penguin's black back and white front are a kind of camouflage. They make it harder for a predator, such as a leopard seal or an orca, to spot it.

Today, warmer weather is melting some of the sea ice that emperor penguins need. Scientists now count penguins using pictures taken from space.

versions.title: Penguins of Antarctica
versions.text:
At the bottom of the world lies Antarctica, a continent buried beneath an enormous sheet of ice. It is the coldest and windiest place on Earth. In winter, the temperature can plunge below minus 40 degrees Celsius, and the sun does not rise for weeks.

Surprisingly, some birds, called penguins, manage to thrive here. Although penguins cannot fly, they are exceptional swimmers. Over millions of years, their wings developed into stiff flippers that propel them through the water.

Penguins have several adaptations for surviving the cold. Beneath their skin is a thick layer of fat called blubber. On top are numerous small feathers packed tightly together, which block the wind and water. During storms, penguins huddle, as hundreds of birds press together and take turns moving into the warm center of the group.

The largest species is the emperor penguin, which stands more than one meter tall. In winter, the female lays a single egg and carefully transfers it to the male. He balances it on his feet, beneath a warm fold of skin, and he eats nothing for approximately two months! Meanwhile, the female travels to the ocean to feed. She returns when the chick hatches, and then both parents feed it.

Penguins consume fish, squid, and krill, which are tiny animals that resemble shrimp. Emperor penguins can dive more than 500 meters deep and hold their breath for about 20 minutes.

A penguin's black back and white front are a type of camouflage. They make it more difficult for a predator, such as a leopard seal or an orca, to notice it.

Today, rising temperatures are melting some of the sea ice that emperor penguins depend on. Scientists now monitor penguin populations using images captured from space.

Meanwhile, the female travels to the ocean to feed, and she returns when the chick hatches so that both parents can feed it.

A penguin's black back and white front are a type of camouflage, which makes it more difficult for a predator, such as a leopard seal or an orca, to notice it in the water.

versions.title: Penguins of Antarctica
versions.text:
At the southern end of the planet lies Antarctica, a continent buried beneath an ice sheet that is, in places, several kilometers thick. It is the coldest, windiest, and driest continent on Earth, and during the polar winter the temperature can plunge below minus 40 degrees Celsius while the sun stays beneath the horizon for weeks at a time.

Remarkably, certain birds not only survive but thrive in this hostile environment. They are penguins, and although these birds cannot fly, they are exceptional swimmers, because over millions of years their wings evolved into stiff, paddle-shaped flippers that propel them through the frigid water.

Penguins depend on a combination of physical and behavioral adaptations to withstand the extreme cold. Beneath their skin lies a thick layer of fat called blubber, which provides insulation against freezing temperatures. Above it, many small, overlapping feathers are packed so tightly together that they block the wind and repel water. During severe storms, penguins huddle, as thousands of birds press together and keep rotating, so that every bird eventually spends time in the sheltered center before returning to the exposed edge.

The largest species is the emperor penguin, which stands more than one meter tall. Unusually, emperors breed during the brutal winter, when the female lays a single egg and carefully transfers it to the male. He must incubate it, balancing it on his feet beneath a special fold of feathered skin. He eats nothing for approximately two months, and he gradually loses a large portion of his body weight. Meanwhile, the female travels to the ocean to feed, and she returns around the time the chick hatches so that both parents can take turns feeding it.

Penguins consume fish, squid, and krill, which are tiny crustaceans that resemble shrimp. Emperor penguins can dive more than 500 meters deep while holding their breath for about 20 minutes.

A penguin's dark back and white front function as camouflage. From above, its back blends with the shadowy depths, while from below, its pale belly matches the bright surface. This combination makes it much harder for a predator, such as a leopard seal or an orca, to detect it.

Today, rising temperatures are melting portions of the sea ice that emperor penguins depend on for breeding. Researchers therefore monitor remote colonies using satellite images, in which the brownish stains left by the birds' droppings reveal their locations.

The chick opened its beak and waited for food.

questions.stem: What is this article mostly about?
options: How to build a home out of ice and snow
How fish swim in the coldest parts of the sea
How penguins live and stay safe in icy Antarctica
Why many birds fly south when winter comes
questions.why: The whole article tells how penguins live in Antarctica: how they swim, stay warm, raise chicks, find food, and hide.

wrong.A: The article is about penguins, not about building homes.
wrong.B: Penguins eat fish, but the article is about penguins.
wrong.D: Penguins cannot fly, and the article does not talk about birds flying south.

questions.stem: What do penguins use their flippers for?
options: To swim
To fly
To dig nests
To keep eggs warm
questions.why: The article says penguins cannot fly and use their flippers to swim.

wrong.B: The article says penguins cannot fly.
wrong.C: The article does not say penguins dig with their flippers.
wrong.D: The father keeps the egg warm on his feet, not with flippers.

questions.stem: Which emperor penguin holds the egg on its feet?
options: The mother
The chick
A seal
The father
questions.why: The article says the mother gives the egg to the father, and he holds it on his feet.

wrong.A: The mother lays the egg, then gives it to the father and goes to the sea.
wrong.B: The chick is inside the egg.
wrong.C: Seals hunt penguins. They do not hold eggs.

questions.stem: The article says penguins huddle in a storm. What does huddle mean?
options: Swim far out into the sea
Stand very close together in a group
Hide alone under the snow
Sleep with their eyes open
questions.why: The article explains that when penguins huddle, they stand close in a big group.

wrong.A: Swimming out to sea is how penguins find food, not how they huddle.
wrong.C: A huddle is a group, not one penguin alone.
wrong.D: The article does not talk about how penguins sleep.

questions.stem: Why do penguins take turns in the middle of the huddle?
options: The middle is the warmest place.
The middle has the most food.
The middle is closest to the sea.
The middle is where the seals hunt.
questions.why: The article calls the middle of the group warm, so taking turns lets each penguin warm up.

wrong.B: There is no food in the huddle.
wrong.C: The article does not say the middle is near the sea.
wrong.D: Seals hunt in the sea, not in the middle of the huddle.

questions.stem: Why does the father penguin not eat for two months?
options: He does not like fish or krill.
There is no food left in the sea.
He must stay with the egg and keep it warm.
He is too small to catch anything.
questions.why: The father holds the egg on his feet the whole time, so he cannot go to the sea to eat.

wrong.A: The article says penguins eat fish, squid, and krill.
wrong.B: The mother goes to the sea to eat, so there is food there.
wrong.D: Emperor penguins are the biggest kind of penguin.

questions.stem: Why are scientists worried that the sea ice is melting?
options: Penguins like to slide on ice for fun.
Ice keeps the seals and whales away.
Melting ice makes the sea too salty.
Penguins could lose a place they need.
questions.why: The article says penguins need the sea ice, so losing it could hurt them.

wrong.A: The article does not say penguins slide for fun.
wrong.B: The article does not say ice keeps hunters away.
wrong.C: The article does not talk about salty water.

questions.stem: Why does the author begin by telling how cold Antarctica is?
options: To tell readers to visit Antarctica
To show how hard it is to live there
To explain how snow is made
To compare Antarctica with Saudi Arabia
questions.why: Starting with the cold, windy land helps readers see why the ways penguins stay warm are so important.

wrong.A: The article does not invite readers to travel there.
wrong.C: The article does not explain how snow forms.
wrong.D: The article does not mention Saudi Arabia.

LOW.prompt: Which way of staying warm do you think helps penguins the most? Explain why, using details from the article.
checklist: I named one way penguins stay warm.
I gave at least two details from the article.
I explained my reason in complete sentences.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the article?

Penguins are the fastest birds that live on Earth.

wrong.A: The article shows that penguins do live in Antarctica.
wrong.B: The article says penguins are good swimmers, not the fastest birds.
wrong.C: Scientists count penguins; the article does not say they want to move them.

More than 500 meters
Only to the bottom of the ice
Less than one meter

wrong.C: The article does not describe diving to the bottom of the ice.
wrong.D: One meter is about how tall an emperor penguin stands.

The bald eagle

wrong.D: Eagles are not mentioned in the article.

questions.stem: The article says a penguin's colors are a kind of camouflage. What does camouflage mean?

A layer of fat under the skin
Colors that help an animal blend in

wrong.A: The article does not describe penguin calls.
wrong.B: A layer of fat under the skin is blubber.
wrong.D: The mother's trip to sea is not camouflage.

It can fly short distances.
Its chick hatches more quickly.

wrong.C: The article says penguins cannot fly.
wrong.D: The colors have nothing to do with hatching.

wrong.B: The article does not say the mother is too small.

questions.stem: Why is melting sea ice a problem for emperor penguins?

keyWords.definition: a machine that circles Earth in space and can take pictures or send signals
keyWords.example: A weather satellite sent images of the storm.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the article?
options: Penguins survive a harsh environment through special adaptations, but warming now threatens their sea ice.
Antarctica is so cold that most penguins migrate to warmer continents every winter.
Emperor penguins are the only species of bird capable of diving deep beneath the ice.
Scientists have discovered that blubber is unnecessary for animals in polar regions.
questions.why: The article explains penguins' physical and behavioral adaptations and ends by describing how melting sea ice affects them.

wrong.B: The article says emperor penguins breed during the winter in Antarctica rather than leaving.
wrong.C: The article describes emperors' deep dives but never says they are the only diving birds.
wrong.D: The article says blubber provides important insulation.

questions.stem: How do researchers locate remote penguin colonies?
options: By following leopard seals through the water
By attaching cameras to every emperor egg
By spotting stains from droppings in satellite images
By listening for penguin calls from research ships
questions.why: The article says researchers use satellite images in which brownish stains from the birds' droppings reveal their locations.

wrong.A: Leopard seals are predators; the article does not say researchers follow them.
wrong.B: The article does not mention cameras on eggs.
wrong.D: The article does not mention listening for calls.

questions.stem: According to the article, how long can emperor penguins hold their breath?
options: About two minutes
About 20 minutes
About two hours
About two months
questions.why: The article states that emperor penguins can hold their breath for about 20 minutes while diving.

wrong.A: The article gives a much longer time than two minutes.
wrong.C: Two hours is far longer than the article states.
wrong.D: Two months is how long the male goes without food.

questions.stem: The article says the male must incubate the egg. What does incubate mean?
options: To carry an egg to the ocean
To break open an egg
To hide an egg from other penguins
To keep an egg warm so it can develop
questions.why: The article explains that the male incubates the egg by balancing it on his feet beneath a warm fold of skin.

wrong.A: The male stays on the ice with the egg; he does not carry it to the ocean.
wrong.B: The chick breaks out when it hatches; incubating keeps the egg whole.
wrong.C: The article does not say the egg is hidden from other penguins.

questions.stem: Why does every penguin in a huddle eventually spend time in the sheltered center?
options: The strongest birds push the weaker ones inside.
The center moves toward the ocean each day.
The birds keep rotating between the center and the edge.
Predators force the penguins to change places.
questions.why: The article explains that the birds continuously rotate, so each one eventually reaches the center before returning to the edge.

wrong.A: The article describes rotation, not pushing by stronger birds.
wrong.B: The article does not say the huddle moves toward the ocean.
wrong.D: Predators are not mentioned as the reason penguins change places.

questions.stem: Why does the male emperor lose a large portion of his body weight?
options: He eats nothing for two months while he incubates the egg.
He dives more deeply than the female during the winter.
His feathers fall out during the coldest storms.
He gives most of his food to the leopard seals.
questions.why: Because he goes without food for about two months while keeping the egg warm, he must live on his stored body fat.

wrong.B: The male stays on the ice during this time; he is not diving.
wrong.C: The article does not say his feathers fall out.
wrong.D: Leopard seals are predators; penguins do not feed them.

questions.stem: What does the word Unusually suggest about emperors breeding in winter?
options: Winter is the easiest season for finding food.
Most chicks in Antarctica hatch in total darkness.
Other penguin species breed only on warmer continents.
Winter is the harshest season for raising an egg.
questions.why: The article describes winter as brutal, with extreme cold and darkness, so breeding then is unexpected.

wrong.A: The female must travel to the ocean to feed, so winter is not easy.
wrong.B: The article does not state where most chicks hatch.
wrong.C: The article does not say where other species breed.

questions.stem: Why does the author end the article with information about satellite images?
options: To argue that penguins should be moved into zoos
To show how scientists track penguins as their habitat changes
To explain how satellites are built and launched
To prove that penguin droppings harm the ice
questions.why: After describing melting sea ice, the author shows how scientists keep watch over remote colonies, linking the threat to the way people study it.

wrong.A: The article never suggests moving penguins to zoos.
wrong.C: The article does not explain how satellites are made.
wrong.D: The droppings are used to find colonies, not to show harm.

HIGH.prompt: Some people say that behaviors, such as huddling, matter more than body features, such as blubber, for penguin survival. Do you agree or disagree? Support your position with evidence from the article.
checklist: I supported it with at least two pieces of evidence from the article.
I explained how my evidence supports my position.
